::: {#exr-prac-exp-mle}
#### Exponential MLE (adapted from @dobson4e, Chapter 3)

Let $X_1, \ldots, X_n \siid \text{Exponential}(\pmean)$,
so that
$$
\p(X = x \mid \pmean) = \frac{1}{\pmean} e^{-x/\pmean},
\quad x > 0, \quad \pmean > 0.
$$

**(a)** Write the log-likelihood $\ell(\pmean; \vx)$
for the observed data $\vx = (x_1, \ldots, x_n)$.

**(b)** Derive the score function $\ell'(\pmean; \vx) = \deriv{\pmean}\ell(\pmean; \vx)$.

**(c)** Set the score equal to zero and show that $\hat\pmean_{ML} = \bar{x}$.
Compute the second derivative and verify this critical point is a maximum.

**(d)** Derive the observed information $\oinf(\pmean; \vx) = -\ell''(\pmean; \vx)$,
evaluate it at $\hat\pmean_{ML}$,
and give an approximate 95% confidence interval for $\pmean$.
:::

:::{#sol-prac-exp-mle}

**(a)**

$$
\ba
\ell(\pmean; \vx)
&= \logf{\prod_{i=1}^n \frac{1}{\pmean} e^{-x_i/\pmean}}
&& \text{(log of the likelihood of an $\iid$ sample)}
\\
&= \sum_{i=1}^n \logf{\frac{1}{\pmean} e^{-x_i/\pmean}}
&& \text{(log of a product)}
\\
&= \sum_{i=1}^n \paren{\logf{\frac{1}{\pmean}} + \logf{e^{-x_i/\pmean}}}
&& \text{(log of a product)}
\\
&= \sum_{i=1}^n \paren{-\logf{\pmean} + \logf{e^{-x_i/\pmean}}}
&& \text{(log of a reciprocal)}
\\
&= \sum_{i=1}^n \paren{-\logf{\pmean} - \frac{x_i}{\pmean}}
&& \text{($\logt$ undoes $\expt$)}
\\
&= \sum_{i=1}^n \paren{-\logf{\pmean}} - \sum_{i=1}^n \frac{x_i}{\pmean}
&& \text{(split the sum)}
\\
&= -n\logf{\pmean} - \sum_{i=1}^n \frac{x_i}{\pmean}
&& \text{(sum of $n$ identical terms)}
\\
&= -n\logf{\pmean} - \frac{1}{\pmean}\sum_{i=1}^n x_i
&& \text{(factor the constant $\tfrac{1}{\pmean}$ out of the sum)}
\\
&= -n\logf{\pmean} - \frac{n\bar{x}}{\pmean}
&& \text{($\textstyle\sum_{i=1}^n x_i = n\bar{x}$)}
\ea
$$

**(b)**

$$
\ba
\ell'(\pmean; \vx)
&= \deriv{\pmean}\paren{-n\logf{\pmean} - \frac{n\bar{x}}{\pmean}}
&& \text{(log-likelihood from (a))}
\\
&= \deriv{\pmean}\paren{-n\logf{\pmean} - n\bar{x}\pmean^{-1}}
&& \text{(write $\tfrac{n\bar{x}}{\pmean}$ as $n\bar{x}\pmean^{-1}$)}
\\
&= \deriv{\pmean}\paren{-n\logf{\pmean}} - \deriv{\pmean}\paren{n\bar{x}\pmean^{-1}}
&& \text{(linearity of differentiation)}
\\
&= -n\deriv{\pmean}\logf{\pmean} - n\bar{x}\deriv{\pmean}\pmean^{-1}
&& \text{(constant multiple rule)}
\\
&= -n\pmean^{-1} - n\bar{x}\deriv{\pmean}\pmean^{-1}
&& \text{(derivative of $\log$)}
\\
&= -n\pmean^{-1} - n\bar{x}\paren{-\pmean^{-2}}
&& \text{(power rule)}
\\
&= -n\pmean^{-1} + n\bar{x}\pmean^{-2}
&& \text{(multiply)}
\\
&= -\frac{n}{\pmean} + \frac{n\bar{x}}{\pmean^2}
&& \text{(write the negative powers as fractions)}
\\
&= -\frac{n\pmean}{\pmean^2} + \frac{n\bar{x}}{\pmean^2}
&& \text{(write both terms over the common denominator)}
\\
&= \frac{-n\pmean + n\bar{x}}{\pmean^2}
&& \text{(combine the fractions)}
\\
&= \frac{n\bar{x} - n\pmean}{\pmean^2}
&& \text{(reorder the numerator)}
\\
&= \frac{n}{\pmean^2}\paren{\bar{x} - \pmean}
&& \text{(factor out $\tfrac{n}{\pmean^2}$)}
\ea
$$

**(c)**

Setting $\ell'(\pmean; \vx) = 0$:

$$
\ba
0 &= \frac{n}{\pmean^2}\paren{\bar{x} - \pmean}
&& \text{(score from (b))}
\\
0 &= \bar{x} - \pmean
&& \text{(multiply both sides by $\tfrac{\pmean^2}{n}$)}
\\
\hat\pmean_{ML} &= \bar{x}
&& \text{(add $\pmean$ to both sides)}
\ea
$$

The second derivative is:

$$
\ba
\ell''(\pmean; \vx)
&= \deriv{\pmean}\paren{-\frac{n}{\pmean} + \frac{n\bar{x}}{\pmean^2}}
&& \text{(score from (b))}
\\
&= \deriv{\pmean}\paren{-n\pmean^{-1} + n\bar{x}\pmean^{-2}}
&& \text{(write the fractions as negative powers)}
\\
&= \deriv{\pmean}\paren{-n\pmean^{-1}} + \deriv{\pmean}\paren{n\bar{x}\pmean^{-2}}
&& \text{(linearity of differentiation)}
\\
&= -n\deriv{\pmean}\pmean^{-1} + n\bar{x}\deriv{\pmean}\pmean^{-2}
&& \text{(constant multiple rule)}
\\
&= -n\paren{-\pmean^{-2}} + n\bar{x}\deriv{\pmean}\pmean^{-2}
&& \text{(power rule for $\pmean^{-1}$)}
\\
&= -n\paren{-\pmean^{-2}} + n\bar{x}\paren{-2\pmean^{-3}}
&& \text{(power rule for $\pmean^{-2}$)}
\\
&= n\pmean^{-2} - 2n\bar{x}\pmean^{-3}
&& \text{(multiply)}
\\
&= \frac{n}{\pmean^2} - \frac{2n\bar{x}}{\pmean^3}
&& \text{(write the negative powers as fractions)}
\ea
$$

Evaluated at $\hat\pmean_{ML} = \bar{x}$:

$$
\ba
\ell''(\bar{x}; \vx)
&= \frac{n}{\bar{x}^2} - \frac{2n\bar{x}}{\bar{x}^3}
&& \text{(second derivative at $\pmean = \bar{x}$)}
\\
&= \frac{n}{\bar{x}^2} - \frac{2n}{\bar{x}^2}
&& \text{(cancel one factor of $\bar{x}$)}
\\
&= -\frac{n}{\bar{x}^2}
&& \text{(combine like terms)}
\ea
$$

Since $n > 0$ and $\bar{x}^2 > 0$, the second derivative is negative,
so $\hat\pmean_{ML} = \bar{x}$ is a maximum.

**(d)**

The observed information is:

$$
\ba
\oinf(\pmean; \vx)
&= -\ell''(\pmean; \vx)
&& \text{(observed information is the negative Hessian)}
\\
&= -\paren{\frac{n}{\pmean^2} - \frac{2n\bar{x}}{\pmean^3}}
&& \text{(second derivative from (c))}
\\
&= -\frac{n}{\pmean^2} + \frac{2n\bar{x}}{\pmean^3}
&& \text{(distribute the minus sign)}
\\
&= \frac{2n\bar{x}}{\pmean^3} - \frac{n}{\pmean^2}
&& \text{(reorder the terms)}
\ea
$$

Evaluated at $\hat\pmean_{ML} = \bar{x}$:

$$
\ba
\oinf(\hat\pmean_{ML}; \vx)
&= \frac{2n\bar{x}}{\bar{x}^3} - \frac{n}{\bar{x}^2}
&& \text{(observed information at $\pmean = \bar{x}$)}
\\
&= \frac{2n}{\bar{x}^2} - \frac{n}{\bar{x}^2}
&& \text{(cancel one factor of $\bar{x}$)}
\\
&= \frac{n}{\bar{x}^2}
&& \text{(combine like terms)}
\ea
$$

So $\SE{\hat\pmean_{ML}} \approx \sqrt{\oinf(\hat\pmean_{ML}; \vx)^{-1}} = \frac{\bar{x}}{\sqrt{n}}$.

An approximate 95% CI for $\pmean$ is:

$$
\hat\pmean_{ML} \pm 1.96 \times \frac{\bar{x}}{\sqrt{n}}
= \bar{x} \pm \frac{1.96\bar{x}}{\sqrt{n}}
$$

Note: the exponential distribution has $\Varf{X} = \pmean^2$,
so $\SE{\hat\pmean_{ML}} = \pmean/\sqrt{n}$,
which is estimated by $\bar{x}/\sqrt{n}$.
More generally,
the standard error of a sample mean is $\SD{X}/\sqrt{n}$;
here that reduces to $\pmean/\sqrt{n}$
because $\SD{X} = \pmean$ for the exponential distribution.

:::
